transcript:
Date: 2026-07-25
Time: 16:00 - 16:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Li (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Elena Morales (Novacore CTO), Samir Gupta (DevOps), Tobias Reed (ML Eng), Jing Wei (Security)

Summary: Quick weekly check-in to review remaining infra gaps preventing canary, confirm access patterns for KMS and VPC, and align on a short smoke test plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya: okay folks thanks for joining. I know we're tight on time so we'll run through the provisioning gaps then canary plan, cool?
[00:00:08] Elena: yep, thanks. We have a couple of blockers still, mostly around KMS access and the private-gateway egress, so hoping to get clarity.
[00:00:16] Jonah: quick note from us — we validated the model binaries and quantized build on our side, everything looks clean. The only perf caveat was at long sequence lengths we saw higher p95, but that's expected until the KV cache warms.
[00:00:30] Samir: sorry interrupt — when you say KV cash, you mean the key value c a c h e? our network folks heard 'cash' and panicked.
[00:00:36] Jonah: yeah sorry, K V cache — kv cache. it's the attention cache that avoids re-compute on context windows.
[00:00:42] Tobias: that matches our expectation. We shipped the same 8-bit quantized weights, and the tokenization matches. The sample prompts I sent earlier should be representative.
[00:00:52] Maya: perfect. Ok first major gap: KMS access. Jing, can you remind the team the compliance requirement here?
[00:00:58] Jing: sure. For PHI-adjacent processing we'll need customer-managed keys with rotate-every-90d and audit logs. Also, certificate-based auth is preferred to short-lived tokens for our auditors.
[00:01:10] Priya: Redwood supports both KMS integrations and bring-your-own-HSM patterns. Jonah, can you summarize the minimal network path for KMS so Samir can validate with infra?
[00:01:20] Jonah: yeah minimal path is outbound TLS to the KMS endpoints on port 443, plus an allowlist for our worker egress IPs. If CB-TLS client certs are required we can do mTLS. The tricky bit is if the key material never leaves HSM — then we do signing calls over network; latency is added per request but acceptable for canary scale.
[00:01:38] Samir: how much latency are we talking about per token if signing is inline?
[00:01:41] Jonah: ballpark an extra 10-25ms per call depending on HSM. But we batch signing, so effective per-token cost is much lower when batching. We'll quantify in the smoke test.
[00:01:50] Elena: we need hard numbers before canary. If that adds too much tail latency, we might want to route low-latency traffic to a cached-key path.
[00:01:58] Maya: noted. Next gap: VPC peering / private gateway. Samir, status?
[00:02:03] Samir: firewall ticket is open, we're waiting on the egress IP list. I have a note to confirm NAT config with networking. Our security team also wants split-tunnel so only inference egress goes to Redwood's VPC.
[00:02:15] Jing: also need flow logs for audit—flow logs at 1 minute granularity if possible.
[00:02:19] Maya: okay we'll provide the egress IP list and recommended flow-log config. I'll attach the sample cloudwatch / stackdriver snippet.
[00:02:26] [00:02:30] Speaker 1: can we talk about tenancy? are we on dedicated or hosted?
[00:02:34] Maya: good q. This POC is running on Redwood Dedicated pool reserved for Novacore, so compute is isolated, but the control plane integration for provisioning still touches the managed plane for metrics. We can transition to private if you need full on-prem.
[00:02:48] Elena: for now dedicated is fine, but we need to ensure logs and audit are exported to our S3 and not retained in Redwood longer than 30 days.
[00:02:56] Priya: we can set retention to 30 days and provide the export pipeline to your S3 using a customer role.
[00:03:03] Tobias: one operational question — when we run a throughput smoke test what are we measuring exactly? GPU util, 99th, p50, p95?
[00:03:09] Jonah: we'll capture P50/P95/P99, GPU util, batch sizes, token throughput, and tail latency. We'll also include the KV hit rate and cache warmup behavior.
[00:03:18] Maya: Jonah will run a 1-hour smoke test once we have KMS and VPC cleared. Tob, you'll provide the prompt set.
[00:03:25] Tobias: yes, I'll prepare a mix: 64-token, 256-token, 512-token prompts, with a 70/30 split of short vs long.
[00:03:32] Samir: are there any ports we need to open inbound?
[00:03:35] Jonah: no inbound required to your cluster — it's all outbound from the dedicated workers to KMS and metrics sinks. The control plane uses HTTPS to report telemetry.
[00:03:43] Elena: what about model fallbacks? if Dedicated capacity spikes, we want automatic fallback to a cheaper variant but same semantics.
[00:03:50] Maya: Redwood supports routing policies — we can define a fallback model with the same decoding behavior but a lower-cost quant. We'll outline a canary policy that tries main model then degradations at token-level thresholds.
[00:04:02] Jing: security question — during fallback, are logs still delivered to our S3 and is there any additional PII exposure?
[00:04:09] Jonah: logs are always routed to your sink. We'll redact any PII at the log level if you prefer — that's configurable.
[00:04:15] Priya: quick note — action items and docs link: https://redwood.ai/pocs/novacore/provisioning (NOTE: placeholder link in notes).
[00:04:23] [00:04:30] Elena: timeline check — we want a canary with 5% production traffic by next week if possible. Is that realistic?
[00:04:36] Maya: aggressive but doable if provisioning drops are closed by Monday. We'll need the KMS keys and firewall confirm by then.
[00:04:44] Samir: I can get the firewall confirm by Sunday evening if you provide the egress list now — but KMS requires sign-off from security.
[00:04:51] Jing: I'll review the KMS method today and share whether we need mTLS or token-based approach. If it's certs we need a CA rotation plan.
[00:04:58] Jonah: small gotcha — if you use client certs we need to provision certs to worker nodes; that process takes an extra day for the image bake and restart.
[00:05:06] Elena: okay factor that in.
[00:05:10] Maya: another piece — observability. We'll add a per-route dashboard with token cost and latency. Priya will configure a shared dashboard view.
[00:05:18] Priya: I'll share the dashboard template after the call.
[00:05:22] [00:05:30] Speaker 1: can we talk about SLA?
[00:05:33] Maya: for Dedicated we have an uptime SLA and latency targets, but during POC we operate under a lighter SLO; final SLA is part of enterprise contract. We'll send a draft SLA doc.
[00:05:44] Tobias: question on caching — how do we ensure KV cache persistence across worker restarts? We had issues in an earlier vendor where cache warmup killed p95 for first 100 requests.
[00:05:53] Jonah: good call. Our runtime supports persistent KV store on local NVMe with quick rehydration and cross-worker sharing for the dedicated pool. But disk persistence depends on your retention policy — if workers are recycled aggressively you will see warmup. We'll suggest autoscale policies that prefer long-lived workers for predictable latency.
[00:06:10] Samir: what's the memory footprint for long-lived caches?
[00:06:13] Jonah: depends on sequence lengths and number of concurrent sessions — we'll include example numbers in the follow-up doc, but estimate 2-4GB per large session, less for shorter contexts.
[00:06:22] Maya: okay, let's move to the actual canary rollout steps so we have a checklist.
[00:06:27] Jonah: proposed canary plan: 1) Provision KMS + VPC allowlist 2) Smoke test 1-hour with representative prompts 3) Canary at 1% traffic for 2 hours 4) Ramp to 5% if metrics good 5) Full rollout with gradual A/B and fallback policy.
[00:06:42] Elena: what are the success criteria for the 1-hour smoke test?
[00:06:46] Maya: success if P95 < 350ms for short prompts, GPU util below 80% stable, and no KMS auth failures. That's negotiable but good baseline.
[00:06:55] Tobias: we'll also add quality checks — ensure output perplexity and token-level correctness for a sample of 100 queries.
[00:07:02] Priya: we'll wire up the eval harness to send comparisons to your QA channel.
[00:07:07] [00:07:15] Speaker 1: any legal or procurement hold-ups?
[00:07:18] Elena: procurement is ready; legal asked for SOC2 attestation and a DPA clause. We sent the redlined DPA last week.
[00:07:25] Maya: got it — legal should have a response by tomorrow.
[00:07:29] Jing: small flag — auditors will ask about key rotation logs; we need to be sure rotation events are visible in the log stream.
[00:07:36] Jonah: rotation events are emitted as structured logs, we'll show sample json in the security doc.
[00:07:41] Samir: network question — if we do split-tunnel, do you need route tables or VPC peering?
[00:07:46] Jonah: split-tunnel typically uses a private gateway in your VPC that proxies outbound calls. We can also set up a peering connection if you prefer direct routing. Both workable.
[00:07:56] Elena: prefer peering for tighter control.
[00:07:58] Maya: action: Maya will share peering instructions and a CloudFormation template for quick setup.
[00:08:05] [00:08:15] Tobias: one last infra detail — do we ship model weights to your dedicated pool or pull from a central registry?
[00:08:20] Jonah: in Dedicated we pull from the Redwood model registry but can replicate the model to local blob storage under your account. If you prefer to hold weights on-prem we can support an air-gap deploy but that's a different cadence.
[00:08:32] Elena: for POC, pulling from registry with encrypted-at-rest storage is fine.
[00:08:37] Maya: ok wrapping up with concrete due dates: Maya to share provisioning checklist by 2026-07-27, Samir to confirm firewall by 2026-07-26, Jing to confirm KMS method by 2026-07-30, Tobias to hand prompt set by 2026-07-28, Jonah to run smoke test by 2026-07-29.
[00:08:57] Priya: I'll slot the security deep-dive next week if Jing wants it.
[00:09:02] Jing: yes please, tentative Wed or Thu.
[00:09:06] Maya: great — any other blockers?
[00:09:09] Samir: none from infra if you give us the lists, we'll move quickly.
[00:09:12] Elena: strong yes from product.
[00:09:15] Maya: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc and a short recap in the next 24 hours.
[00:09:21] [00:09:30] Speaker 1: thanks all bye.

--- End Transcript ---
questions: Will KMS inline signing add unacceptable tail latency?
Is peering preferred over split-tunnel for Novacore?
What are the exact SLA targets for canary vs production?
notes: AE recommended CloudFormation template for peering to be provided
Jonah to include KV cache memory footprint examples in follow-up
